concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly sets up compound growth, cancels the principal, uses the logarithm power rule, solves t = ln(2)/ln(1.08) ≈ 9.006 and explains each step pedagogically, whereas Lesson 2 has no available transcript or script to verify any mathematical accuracy or instructional clarity.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner. Four high-confidence agents favor it: interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy all strongly prefer Lesson 1, with confidences around 0.98–0.99. These dimensions indicate that Lesson 1 has a functioning quiz gate, clear narration, mostly aligned visual timing, and mathematically correct/pedagogically sound treatment of compound interest. Lesson 2 wins visual accuracy and polish with moderate-to-high confidence because it is more legible and avoids Lesson 1’s clipping, misalignment, and layout bugs. However, Lesson 2 lacks available narration, sync data, interactivity, and verifiable instructional script, so its strengths are mostly visual while Lesson 1 is substantially stronger instructionally. The weighted evidence strongly favors Lesson 1 despite its visual polish problems.
